113	## Rebuilding the binary base

145	## Startup dependencies
146	
147	Managed GRPO starts judge loading, Ray startup, and workflow model/data preparation
148	concurrently after assigning GPUs and discovering judge endpoint addresses. Ray
149	readiness and judge known-answer canaries run in separate supervised subprocesses.
150	The driver waits for the exact Ray layout before placement; it waits for judge
151	qualification before generation or evaluation. Readiness files live in the fresh
152	attempt directory, with peer-failure propagation. After replica rendezvous, rank
153	zero writes one `startup.json` deadline shared by all supervisors, readiness
154	probes, and driver barriers. Inventory and service launch consume that same
155	budget; starting a later stage does not reset it. Post-training completion has
156	its own timeout.
157	
158	On disaggregated runs with an explicit rollout count and resident inference,
159	trainer initialization/cache restoration overlaps inference initialization.
160	Connecting trainer parallelism metadata and restoring the rollout cursor remains
161	a barrier after both branches finish, before initial weight publication. Colocated,
162	offloaded-inference, and epoch-derived schedules retain sequential initialization.
163	OPD uses its separate launcher and does not pass through this GRPO supervisor.
164	
165	A failed or cancelled initialization joins its sibling tasks before driver cleanup;
166	the worker manager owns partially initialized remote workers. Cluster supervision
167	also terminates outstanding readiness subprocesses. Judge liveness monitoring
168	starts only after its HTTP endpoint becomes ready.

171	timestamps. Each probe writes its own timeline under `ray-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`
172	or `judge-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`, avoiding concurrent appends on WEKA. The run

174	module import, readiness waits, serving/trainer initialization, connection and
175	publication timings. Overlapping stage durations must not be added together as
176	elapsed startup time. Small-model integration validates ordering and cleanup;
177	full-model wall-time savings require measurement on the intended hardware.

188	The moved adapter is checked against that Core API in the dedicated runtime
189	environment; Open Instruct's ordinary type check covers the application integration.

271	## Adapter package layout
272	
273	`open_instruct/miles/` groups code by responsibility. The public CLI remains
274	`python -m open_instruct.miles`; package initializers do not load the GPU runtime.
275	
276	| Package | Responsibility |
277	|---|---|
278	| `configuration` | RunSpec/CoreConfig, native options, validation, topology and capacity planning |
279	| `execution` | Preparation, Beaker submission, cluster bootstrap and training coordination |
280	| MILES `backends/core_utils` | Core actor, model backends, packing, optimizer scheduling, checkpoints and trainer diagnostics |
281	| `rollout` | Application data-source selection and rollout metrics; managed generation, admission and completed queues live in MILES `backends/core_utils/rollout` |
282	| MILES `backends/core_utils/publication` | Weight delivery, engine drain, policy versions and durable policy state |
283	| `rewards` | Verifiers, reward routing and managed judges |
284	| `datasets` | Dataset preparation, mixtures, inference records and prompt selection |
285	| `evaluation` | Background evaluation submission, workers and result publication |
286	| `infrastructure` | Application artifact publication and bounded infrastructure waits; compiler/HF cache lifecycle lives in MILES |
287	
288	Keep diagnostics next to the component they observe. Keep configuration imports
289	CPU-only, model backends loaded on demand, and package initializers minimal.
290	MILES `backends/core_utils/data.py` adapts samples to the trainer; `rollout/data_source.py` owns
291	runtime data-source behavior; `datasets/run_data.py` prepares researcher inputs.
292	
293	Python integration imports use these package paths, for example
294	`from open_instruct.miles.configuration.run_spec import RunSpec`. The pinned
295	AllenAI MILES fork must use the matching trainer and rollout hook paths. Rebuild
296	the application image when updating this layout and its runtime pin together;
297	existing images retain their original code. Custom verifier factories and saved
298	native options must reference these package paths.
299	
300	The CPU CLI checks in `open_instruct/test_miles_package_layout.py` run without
301	site-packages. `tests/miles/test_package_layout.py` resolves hooks supplied by
302	both repositories inside the pinned runtime.
303	
304	### Application callbacks and CPU tools
305	
306	The backend trainer and managed rollout modules do not import Open Instruct.
307	Open Instruct supplies `core_records_factory` for per-question recording and
308	`core_evaluation_snapshot` for requested post-update HF exports. Those callbacks
309	preserve the existing recording and evaluation schedules. Dataset preparation,
310	reward callbacks, data-source selection, Beaker launch and evaluation submission
311	remain application-owned. The native `olmo_core` argument loader still resolves
312	Open Instruct's run configuration; that is an explicit configuration integration.
313	
314	Small CPU planning and artifact-reader helpers remain local so `plan`, `validate`
315	and offline analysis work without the private runtime. Runtime integration tests
316	compare their algorithms with the MILES counterparts: scoring policy, capacity
317	reporting, timeout diagnostics, atomic JSON publication, input validation and
318	throughput arithmetic.
319	
320	## Core runtime compatibility
321	
322	The `olmo-core` revision in
323	[`runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json) is the Core source used
324	by the runtime. The adapter interfaces it relies on were merged in
325	[OLMo-core PR #888](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/pull/888). The runtime pins
326	merge commit `6ceda6530625caa5d23e3be8a455c600f62a7338`, including the reviewed
327	RoPE import fixes, alongside the MILES v0.1.2 integration.
328	
329	Core's routed-expert `match_eager_rounding` defaults to false. The pinned MILES
330	adapter explicitly enables it for policy scoring and accepts legacy MILES
331	checkpoint manifests with equivalent scoring semantics. Other Core users keep
332	the default behavior.
333	
334	Core's PR checks and application validation cover different boundaries.
335	Rebuild runtime/application images from the lock and validate the intended
336	training topology; an existing image retains its original source revisions.
337	Record application validation with the exact image and source pins. The compact
338	options snapshot must be regenerated whenever runtime source pins change.

145	## Startup dependencies
146	
147	Managed GRPO starts judge loading, Ray startup, and workflow model/data preparation
148	concurrently after assigning GPUs and discovering judge endpoint addresses. Ray
149	readiness and judge known-answer canaries run in separate supervised subprocesses.
150	The driver waits for the exact Ray layout before placement; it waits for judge
151	qualification before generation or evaluation. Readiness files live in the fresh
152	attempt directory, with peer-failure propagation. After replica rendezvous, rank
153	zero writes one `startup.json` deadline shared by all supervisors, readiness
154	probes, and driver barriers. Inventory and service launch consume that same
155	budget; starting a later stage does not reset it. Post-training completion has
156	its own timeout.
157	
158	On disaggregated runs with an explicit rollout count and resident inference,
159	trainer initialization/cache restoration overlaps inference initialization.
160	Connecting trainer parallelism metadata and restoring the rollout cursor remains
161	a barrier after both branches finish, before initial weight publication. Colocated,
162	offloaded-inference, and epoch-derived schedules retain sequential initialization.
163	OPD uses its separate launcher and does not pass through this GRPO supervisor.
164	
165	A failed or cancelled initialization joins its sibling tasks before driver cleanup;
166	the worker manager owns partially initialized remote workers. Cluster supervision
167	also terminates outstanding readiness subprocesses. Judge liveness monitoring
168	starts only after its HTTP endpoint becomes ready.
169	
170	For measurement, the attempt directory contains process start receipts, readiness
171	timestamps. Each probe writes its own timeline under `ray-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`
172	or `judge-readiness/driver_timing.jsonl`, avoiding concurrent appends on WEKA. The run
173	root has preparation-stage timings; the checkpoint directory has runtime parsing,
174	module import, readiness waits, serving/trainer initialization, connection and
175	publication timings. Overlapping stage durations must not be added together as
176	elapsed startup time. Small-model integration validates ordering and cleanup;
177	full-model wall-time savings require measurement on the intended hardware.

179	## Local development
180	
181	The ordinary CPU suite covers configuration, planning, launch specifications,
182	rewards, data preparation, rendezvous, heartbeat, recovery and topology contracts
183	without installing MILES or

185	checks application types without requiring the private runtime.

187	Open Instruct keeps record configuration tests and runtime selection/buffer integration tests.
188	The moved adapter is checked against that Core API in the dedicated runtime
189	environment; Open Instruct's ordinary type check covers the application integration.

191	lock. The ordinary `uv.lock` Core version is for existing SFT/DPO paths and is

208	therefore does not check GPU kernels, distributed gradients or publication.

262	In a development environment with the pinned MILES and Core sources, run:

266	```

269	application image and runtime tests check both repositories together.

271	## Adapter package layout
272	
273	`open_instruct/miles/` groups code by responsibility. The public CLI remains
274	`python -m open_instruct.miles`; package initializers do not load the GPU runtime.
275	
276	| Package | Responsibility |
277	|---|---|
278	| `configuration` | RunSpec/CoreConfig, native options, validation, topology and capacity planning |
279	| `execution` | Preparation, Beaker submission, cluster bootstrap and training coordination |
280	| MILES `backends/core_utils` | Core actor, model backends, packing, optimizer scheduling, checkpoints and trainer diagnostics |
281	| `rollout` | Application data-source selection and rollout metrics; managed generation, admission and completed queues live in MILES `backends/core_utils/rollout` |
282	| MILES `backends/core_utils/publication` | Weight delivery, engine drain, policy versions and durable policy state |
283	| `rewards` | Verifiers, reward routing and managed judges |
284	| `datasets` | Dataset preparation, mixtures, inference records and prompt selection |
285	| `evaluation` | Background evaluation submission, workers and result publication |
286	| `infrastructure` | Application artifact publication and bounded infrastructure waits; compiler/HF cache lifecycle lives in MILES |
287	
288	Keep diagnostics next to the component they observe. Keep configuration imports
289	CPU-only, model backends loaded on demand, and package initializers minimal.
290	MILES `backends/core_utils/data.py` adapts samples to the trainer; `rollout/data_source.py` owns
291	runtime data-source behavior; `datasets/run_data.py` prepares researcher inputs.
292	
293	Python integration imports use these package paths, for example
294	`from open_instruct.miles.configuration.run_spec import RunSpec`. The pinned
295	AllenAI MILES fork must use the matching trainer and rollout hook paths. Rebuild
296	the application image when updating this layout and its runtime pin together;
297	existing images retain their original code. Custom verifier factories and saved
298	native options must reference these package paths.
299	
300	The CPU CLI checks in `open_instruct/test_miles_package_layout.py` run without
301	site-packages. `tests/miles/test_package_layout.py` resolves hooks supplied by
302	both repositories inside the pinned runtime.
303	
304	### Application callbacks and CPU tools
305	
306	The backend trainer and managed rollout modules do not import Open Instruct.
307	Open Instruct supplies `core_records_factory` for per-question recording and
308	`core_evaluation_snapshot` for requested post-update HF exports. Those callbacks
309	preserve the existing recording and evaluation schedules. Dataset preparation,
310	reward callbacks, data-source selection, Beaker launch and evaluation submission
311	remain application-owned. The native `olmo_core` argument loader still resolves
312	Open Instruct's run configuration; that is an explicit configuration integration.
313	
314	Small CPU planning and artifact-reader helpers remain local so `plan`, `validate`
315	and offline analysis work without the private runtime. Runtime integration tests
316	compare their algorithms with the MILES counterparts: scoring policy, capacity
317	reporting, timeout diagnostics, atomic JSON publication, input validation and
318	throughput arithmetic.
319	
320	## Core runtime compatibility
321	
322	The `olmo-core` revision in
323	[`runtime.lock.json`](../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json) is the Core source used
324	by the runtime. The adapter interfaces it relies on were merged in
325	[OLMo-core PR #888](https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core/pull/888). The runtime pins
326	merge commit `6ceda6530625caa5d23e3be8a455c600f62a7338`, including the reviewed
327	RoPE import fixes, alongside the MILES v0.1.2 integration.
328	
329	Core's routed-expert `match_eager_rounding` defaults to false. The pinned MILES
330	adapter explicitly enables it for policy scoring and accepts legacy MILES
331	checkpoint manifests with equivalent scoring semantics. Other Core users keep
332	the default behavior.
333	
334	Core's PR checks and application validation cover different boundaries.
335	Rebuild runtime/application images from the lock and validate the intended
336	training topology; an existing image retains its original source revisions.
337	Record application validation with the exact image and source pins. The compact
338	options snapshot must be regenerated whenever runtime source pins change.

1	# MILES researcher workflow
2	
3	A run file describes the checkpoint, data, trainer, serving engines, objective,
4	logging and allocation together. The section names follow the Megatron implementation;
5	the resolved training backend here is OLMo-core. Existing `[core]` / `[miles]`
6	TOMLs and the `RunConfig` Python interface remain available for low-level work.
7	
8	Choose a maintained [starting point](../../configs/miles/examples/README.md),
9	then copy it into ignored `runs/` before customizing it. The
10	[generated recipe tables](configuration.md#example-recipes) describe the current
11	allocations and batch geometry.
12	
13	Replace `YOUR_USERNAME` and the checkpoint path before launching. A model source
14	must include the compatible architecture, tokenizer and chat template. Keep the
15	source read-only and give each run a new output directory. The colocated example
16	requires a tiny model that fits alongside its optimizer and engine; it does not
17	establish full-SFT colocation support.
18	
19	HF inputs must contain `config.json`, safetensors weights and a usable tokenizer
20	with a chat template. Native Core conversion exports checkpoint metadata and
21	weights using the Core converter with forward validation disabled, so it is
22	not a numerical or routing-parity check; architecture-specific conversion and
23	serving checks remain separate. HF staging references source
24	weights, so retain the original checkpoint for the life of the run.
25	
26	## One configuration, inspection through launch
27	
28	```bash
29	python -m open_instruct.miles plan configs/miles/examples/node.toml
30	python -m open_instruct.miles validate configs/miles/examples/node.toml
31	```
32	
33	`plan` resolves the structured sections into the existing Core configuration and
34	native MILES arguments without allocating GPUs. Inspect model paths, data
35	sources, placement, batch geometry and objective before submission. `validate`
36	checks the structured configuration on a CPU host; native MILES validation also
37	runs before training in the pinned runtime. Neither proves memory fit or learning
38	quality.
39	
40	Use `train` inside an allocation. `run` launches the config-driven Beaker
41	workflow and `status` inspects the submitted run:
42	
43	```bash
44	python -m open_instruct.miles run runs/my-run.toml
45	python -m open_instruct.miles status runs/my-run.toml
46	```
47	
48	See the complete [laptop and Beaker-session launch guide](launching.md).
49	
50	`run` delegates image building and submission to the repository's committed
51	`scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh --miles` workflow. First commit the
52	working tree and set `MILES_BASE_IMAGE` to the locally loaded base image recorded
53	in `runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json`. Alternatively, set `MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE`
54	to a compatible immutable Beaker image ID; aliases are rejected. The submitting
55	host needs the Beaker CLI and credentials, plus Docker when building.
56	
57	The config launcher supports single-node runs and replicated disaggregated
58	allocations with independent trainer, rollout and named-judge GPU counts.
59	See [multi-node placement and managed judges](managed-judges.md) for the
60	ownership rules, limits and a tiny example configuration. `plan` reports
61	per-node assignments and unused GPUs. Multi-node runs may keep
62	`launch.auto_resume=true`: a restart into the same output root resumes from the
63	newest native checkpoint and continues the rollout cursor without repeating or
64	skipping an update. Forced multi-node preemption, and restarts of runs carrying
65	a managed judge, are untested.
66	
67	`status` reports the latest Beaker attempt, all experiment details and whether
68	the current config matches the submitted config. Receipts live under
69	`~/.cache/open-instruct/miles/launches` by default; set `MILES_LAUNCH_RECEIPTS`
70	to use another directory. It does not read live training metrics from WEKA.
71	
72	Preparation and resolved settings are retained under the run root. `workflow.json` records `preparing`, `training`,
73	`complete` or `failed`; logs and small JSON reports are also collected into
74	Beaker results. Checkpoints and rollout tensors remain on WEKA. Reusing an
75	output root requires an unchanged run specification; completed runs cannot be overwritten. With `auto_resume=true`,

## 3. Configuration and launching

One structured TOML (`configs/miles/examples/{dev,node,three-node}.toml`, `schema_version=1`). CLI: `python -m open_instruct.miles {plan,validate,train,run|status} run.toml` with repeatable `--set SECTION.KEY=TOML_VALUE`. `plan`/`validate` are CPU-only; `train` runs inside an allocation; `run` delegates to the committed `scripts/train/build_image_and_launch.sh --miles` via `execution/launch.py`, submitting a Beaker experiment with GPU placement/mounts/replicas and storing receipts under `~/.cache/open-instruct/miles/launches`. Images: `scripts/miles/build_image.py`, `build_base_image.py`, `prepare_runtime.py`; env `MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE`/`MILES_BASE_IMAGE`. `scripts/miles/` also has analysis tools (`analyze_engine_drain.py`, `analyze_throughput.py`, `capacity_metrics.py`), doc generation (`generate_docs.py`, `snapshot_options.py`, `capture_option_help.py`), and evaluation helpers.

## 4. Rewards/verifiers and OLMo-core relation

`core.reward_config` points to a trusted JSON registry mapping verifier names → `{"factory": "package.Class", "config": {...}}`; samples carry only names/weights/targets in `metadata.verifiers`, so data cannot choose arbitrary code (`rewards/rewards.py` docstring). Verifiers run isolated with timeouts. In contrast, `open_instruct/grpo_olmo_core_actor.py` is the **older, non-MILES** OLMo-core path: `PolicyTrainerOLMoCoreProcess` (Ray actor, line 46) + `OLMoCoreModelGroup` (line 426), using vLLM NCCL weight transfer and Open Instruct's own GRPO callbacks — it contains no MILES references. MILES replaces this with the pinned runtime's `miles.backends.core_utils.actor.OLMoCoreTrainRayActor`, coordinated by `execution/driver.py`.
